'''Herbert Bishop Keller''' (19 June 1925 in [[Paterson, New Jersey]] – 26 January 2008 in [[Pasadena, California]])<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Herbert Bishop Keller (1925-2008) |url=https://shellbuckling.com/cv/kellerhb.pdf}}</ref> was an American [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[numerical analysis|numerical analyst]]. He was professor of applied mathematics, emeritus, at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name="caltech_obit">{{cite web|url=http://eands.caltech.edu/articles/LXXI-1/keller.html |title=Obituary: Herbert B. Keller |publisher=[[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] |accessdate=2009-09-21 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100625001138/http://eands.caltech.edu/articles/LXXI-1/keller.html |archivedate=2010-06-25 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Keller graduated from the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]] with a bachelor's in electrical engineering in 1945; and from [[New York University]], later known as the [[Courant Institute]], with a Ph.D. in 1954.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://oralhistories.library.caltech.edu/151/|title=Interview with Herbert B. Keller|work=Oral History Project|publisher=[[California Institute of Technology]] Archives|year=1998|accessdate=2011-07-10}}</ref>

==Career==
A Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], Keller was known for his contributions to the field of applied mathematics and [[numerical analysis]] including [[bifurcation theory]], [[computational fluid dynamics]] (CFD), and [[scientific computing]]. He is the co-author, with [[Eugene Isaacson]], of the classic textbook ''Analysis of Numerical Methods'', which is still in use in leading graduate programs in applied mathematics.<ref name="siamnews">{{cite web|url=http://siam.tekdevelopment.com/old-issues/2008/julyaugust-2008/obituary-herbert-keller/ |title=Obituary: Herbert Keller |publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] |accessdate=2009-09-21 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716202912/http://siam.tekdevelopment.com/old-issues/2008/julyaugust-2008/obituary-herbert-keller/ |archivedate=2011-07-16 }}</ref> 
It is interesting to observe that the first letters of each sentence in the Preface spell "Down With Computers And Their Lackeys."
He served as president of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (1974–1976).<ref>SIAM Presidents http://www.siam.org/about/more/presidents.php</ref>

Keller was a recipient of the [[Theodore von Kármán Prize]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] in 1994.<ref name="latimes">{{cite news|url=https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/latimes/access/59270516.html?dids=59270516:59270516&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Jan+6%2C+1994&author=&pub=Los+Angeles+Times+(pre-1997+Fulltext)&edition=&startpage=5&desc=PEOPLE|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022192524/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/latimes/access/59270516.html?dids=59270516:59270516&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Jan+6,+1994&author=&pub=Los+Angeles+Times+(pre-1997+Fulltext)&edition=&startpage=5&desc=PEOPLE|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 22, 2012|title=People|date=1884-01-06|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|accessdate=2009-09-21}}</ref> Herbert was the younger brother of applied mathematician [[Joseph Keller|Joseph B. Keller]].<ref name="keller_interview">{{cite web|url=http://oralhistories.library.caltech.edu/151/01/Keller_OHO.pdf|title=Interview: Herbert B. Keller |year=1996|publisher=Caltech library|accessdate=2009-09-21}}</ref>  Joseph Keller was also a co-advisor for Herbert's PhD thesis.

Keller was an avid bicyclist even at 82 years old. He died after his regular Saturday morning bike ride when he took a dip in a hot tub to relax his muscles, lost consciousness due to hyperthermia, and drowned.
